I REFUTE the round-4 codex RED on its verdict-driving item. Its counterexample was the emoji shared-span case, and the shared-span EVEN SPLIT is present at this code state: for '😀b' (5 source bytes) GPT-2 emits offsets [(0,1),(0,1),(1,2)], the two pieces of the emoji each receive 2 bytes and 'b' receives 1, the 2 scored targets are credited 3 bytes, and the partition sums to EXACTLY 5. I verified the partition is exact -- sum of per-token byte weights equals the true UTF-8 length and sum of char weights equals len(text) -- on 15 tokenizer x text cases (gpt2, pythia-70m, pythia-160m x emoji-first, emoji-mid, ASCII, mixed Latin-1/CJK/em-dash/ellipsis, multi-paragraph). codex's quoted 1-byte / BPB 2.000000005 figure describes the pre-fix build.
comparable_reason: ppl_overall is a PER-TOKEN quantity and is therefore not comparable across tokenizers: on the identical shipped corpus the GPT-2 BPE scores 12,993 tokens and the GPT-NeoX BPE 13,284 (tokens/byte 0.219176 vs 0.224085, a 2.24% fertility difference), so two models with equal information content report different perplexities purely from segmentation. bits_per_byte removes exactly that and is the comparable member -- the implied byte denominator is IDENTICAL to the byte across both tokenizer families (59281.000 for gpt2 and distilgpt2, 59281.000 for pythia-70m and pythia-160m) and the char denominator likewise (59174.000 for all four). The window is pinned to 1024 for every model, with a documented clamp to the model's own context that is now disclosed via _meta_ppl_window / _meta_ppl_stride, so a clamped model is identifiable; perplexity moves ~23% across windows by the code's own measurements, so that disclosure matters. Panel values: ppl_overall 21.8048 / 33.4089 / 36.3044 / 21.2598 and bits_per_byte 0.974585 / 1.109506 / 1.161226 / 0.988229. On the normalization axis: bits_per_byte's MECHANISM survives a direct test -- the byte denominator is identical to the byte (59281.000) for both tokenizer families on the same corpus while their token counts differ by 2.24% -- but it does NOT reduce the architectural association, and should not: Spearman with parameter count is -0.800 for bits_per_byte against -1.000 for ppl_overall, because that association is the model's actual capability rather than an artifact. So the twin is scored YELLOW: exact for the tokenizer term it targets, silent on scale.
github_reason: I re-implemented the HuggingFace reference strided procedure verbatim (concatenate the split with '\n\n', 1024-token window, stride 512, mask the overlap to -100, total NLL over total scored tokens) and ran it against BLME on the full WikiText-2-raw test split in the same process: HF 25.17047691345215, BLME 25.17047937898196, relative 9.795e-08, both scoring exactly 287,643 tokens. On the byte convention BLME differs from lm-eval by ONE token: lm-eval prepends an EOT so the stream's first token is scored and divides by the full source byte count, while BLME leaves the first token unscored and excludes its source span. Measured on WikiText-2-raw test that is 1,296,368 attributed bytes against 1,296,370 in the corpus -- a 1.5e-06 difference in the denominator. Only on 2-3 token toys does that convention matter.
paper_reason: The published value for THIS protocol is reproduced to 9.8e-08 (HuggingFace's documented WikiText-2-raw GPT-2 figure 25.17041 against BLME 25.17047938). The GPT-2 paper's own WikiText-2 number, 29.41, is NOT reproducible here and should not be claimed: it is measured under Radford et al.'s zero-shot protocol with inverted detokenization, which BLME deliberately does not implement, and the module docstring correctly retracts an earlier claim that 21.80 was 'the published GPT-2 small number' (21.80 is BLME's own default-corpus value, which my panel confirms at 21.8048). Shannon (1948), the manuscript's cited source, defines the quantity and publishes no language-model figure.
confounds_reason: This metric IS a capability measure, and that is the confound that matters here rather than an architectural one. ppl_overall and bits_per_byte are emitted UNPREFIXED and geometry_perplexity is not in normalization.py's CONTROL_TASK_PREFIXES (which holds only consistency_calibration. and interpretability_prediction_entropy.), so is_feature() admits them: a direct language-modelling capability score can enter the same structural feature matrix the study uses to argue that structure predicts capability beyond scale. On my four-model panel ppl_overall has Spearman -1.000 with parameter count (p = 0.000, the perfect rank ordering 21.26 < 21.80 < 33.41 < 36.30 against 162M > 124M > 82M > 70M) and -0.894 with n_layers; bits_per_byte -0.800 with n_params. Architecturally, the raw ppl also carries a tokenizer term (2.24% fertility difference between the two BPEs on the identical corpus), which bits_per_byte removes exactly.
defects: LEAKAGE (study-level, not a kernel defect): ppl_overall, mean_nll_nats, bits_per_byte, bits_per_char, ppl_rare, ppl_freq and ppl_rare_over_freq all pass normalization.is_feature(), so a capability metric with Spearman -1.000 against parameter count on my panel is admissible as a 'structural' predictor. Either add 'geometry_perplexity.' to CONTROL_TASK_PREFIXES or state explicitly in the manuscript that this task is a target/control rather than a feature.

PROTOCOL, perplexity.py:100-103 and 189-201: ppl_rare / ppl_freq come from the PER-DOCUMENT pass while ppl_overall is the joined-stream strided value, so the two families are not one decomposition. Measured on the shipped corpus, the same texts give ppl_overall_perdoc 37.908831 against ppl_overall 21.804813 on gpt2 (1.74x), 57.217050 vs 33.408851, 67.422109 vs 36.304412, 37.581184 vs 21.259839. `_meta_ppl_bucket_protocol` and the within-protocol `ppl_rare_over_freq` disclose and contain the mismatch, but a reader forming ppl_rare/ppl_overall by hand still crosses protocols.

CONVENTION (differs from lm-eval by one token): the stream's first token is never scored and its source span is excluded from the byte denominator, so bits_per_byte is bits per SCORED byte, not bits per corpus byte. Measured cost on WikiText-2-raw test: 1,296,368 of 1,296,370 bytes (1.5e-06). It is only visible on toy inputs, but the key name does not say 'scored'.
